page: Amazon Web Services m8gn.large is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs built on the ARMv9 arm64 architecture utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V2 processor running at 2.8 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache, with hardware acceleration for AES encryption. The instance provides 8.0 GB of system memory, matching the standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of general-purpose instances, and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps. There is no bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results demonstrate solid single-thread execution, highlighted by a strong bzip3 single-threaded decompression rate of 14.33 GB/sec and average tier performance in stress-ng single-core (1707.18) and Geekbench single-core (1820.0). However, overall aggregate throughput is constrained by its low core count. Multi-threaded metrics register in lower tiers, including multi-core Geekbench (3246.0), multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (28.42 GB/sec), and PassMark CPU overall score (1542.47). Large-block uncached read memory bandwidth reaches 56.64 GB/sec, while write operations peak at 23.11 GB/sec.

Given its two dedicated cores and moderate memory allocation, the instance represents an efficient entry-level profile for workloads requiring consistent single-thread responsiveness without high multi-core concurrency. It is well matched for lightweight web servers, microservices, background job workers, small-scale database operations, and development environments that rely on external EBS volumes for storage.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gn.large is a general-purpose, Nitro-based virtual server powered by 2 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores operating at 2.8 GHz. Configured with 8.0 GB of RAM and 6 Gbps baseline network throughput, this instance delivers balanced compute-to-memory resources without bundled local storage or hardware accelerators. Benchmark evaluations reveal competent single-core processing capabilities, such as a strong 14.33 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression and mid-tier Geekbench single-core execution of 1820.0. The low total core count naturally limits parallel processing throughput, placing multi-threaded stress-ng and PassMark metrics into lower performance brackets. Lacking local storage, the instance relies on remote network storage for persistence. It provides an efficient computing footprint for small application backends, API gateways, low-traffic web hosting, and lightweight development tasks.
